Complete the tracking of the period a cycle in a scalogram

Source: R/completed_series.R
completed_series.Rd

Use the traced series and the existing wavelet or superlet scalogram to complete the tracking of a cycle in scalogram. The selected points using the track_period_wavelet or track_period function form a incomplete line unless every point is tracked. However clicking every individual point along a wavelet ridge is time intensive and error prone. To avoid errors and save time the completed_series function can be used to complete the tracing of a cycle in a wavelet spectra. The completed_series function interpolates the data points selected using the track_period_wavelet or track_period. A a search a algorithm then looks up and replaces the interpolated curve values with the values of the nearest spectral peak in the wavelet spectra.

Usage

completed_series(
  scalogram = NULL,
  tracked_curve = NULL,
  period_up = 1.2,
  period_down = 0.8,
  extrapolate = TRUE,
  genplot = FALSE,
  keep_editable = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

scalogram

Scalogram in which the cycle was tracked: the output of analyse_wavelet (class analyze.wavelet) or of analyse_superlet (class analyze.superlet). Its depth axis sets the positions of the completed curve. Required (Default=NULL gives an error).

tracked_curve

Incomplete tracked period curve (matrix or data frame, two columns: depth in column 1 and the tracked period in column 2, in the depth units of the scalogram), e.g. the output of track_period_wavelet or track_period; rows with NA are dropped. It is linearly interpolated onto the depth axis of the scalogram before the search for spectral peaks. Required (Default=NULL gives an error).

period_up

Factor (numeric, > 1) that sets the upper limit of the search window: at every depth the nearest spectral peak (local power maximum along the period axis) is used only if its period is below the interpolated period times period_up; otherwise no value is assigned there (see extrapolate). Default=1.2.

period_down

Factor (numeric, between 0 and 1) that sets the lower limit of the search window: the nearest spectral peak is used only if its period is above the interpolated period times period_down. Default=0.8.

extrapolate

Fill the depths where no spectral peak was found within the window by linear interpolation between the found values (with the first and last found values held constant towards the ends) (logical, TRUE or FALSE); FALSE leaves NA at those depths. Default=TRUE.

genplot

Plot the completed curve (red) together with the original tracked curve (black) (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

keep_editable

Keep the graphical parameters of the plot so that extra elements can be added afterwards (logical, TRUE or FALSE); FALSE restores the previous par settings. Default=FALSE.

...

Arguments of older versions: wavelet is accepted as an alias of scalogram; other arguments are ignored.

Value

Returns a matrix with 2 columns The first column is the depth axis The second column is the completed tracking of the period a cycle of the wavelet spectra

Examples

# \donttest{
#Use the grey_track example points to complete the tracking of the
# precession cycle in the wavelet spectra of the grey scale data set
# of Zeeden et al., (2013).



grey_wt <-
 analyse_wavelet(
   data = grey,
   dj = 1/200,
   lowerPeriod = 0.02,
   upperPeriod = 256,
   verbose = FALSE,
   omega_nr = 8
 )

#The ~22kyr precession cycle is between 0.25 and 1m The grey_track data
#set is a pre-loaded uncompleted tracking of the precession cycle

#grey_track <- track_period_wavelet(
#astro_cycle = 22,
#wavelet = NULL,
#n.levels = 100,
#periodlab = "Period (meters)",
#x_lab = "depth (meters)"
#)



grey_track <- completed_series(
 scalogram = grey_wt,
 tracked_curve  = grey_track,
 period_up  = 1.25,
 period_down  = 0.75,
 extrapolate = TRUE,
genplot = FALSE,
keep_editable=FALSE
)
# }
